newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Henry Walker targets further growth 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Henry Walker targets further growth 97/98.

text.p: Contract mining and engineering group Henry Walker Ltd said on Wednesday it had entered the 1997/98 financial year which began on July 1 well-placed and seeking to achieve further growth during the year.
The company earlier announced its net profit in the year to June 30 rose to A$20.99 million from A$17.70 million the previous year.
Henry Walker said the company would target a 10 percent rise in revenue and earnings in 1997/98.

"The outlook for 1998 and beyond is positive, supported by the strength of the company's year-end order book position and the activity levels anticipated for the Australian minerals and infrastructure sectors," it said in its results announcement.
Henry Walker recorded an 18 percent rise in net profit to A$20.9 million for the year to June 30, with total revenue up 23 percent to A$543.8 million.
The company said that as of June 30 it had work in hand of A$300 million for 1997/98, compared to A$275 million at the start of the year.

"Henry Walker anticipates that activity levels in the development of mineral and infrastructure projects and the ongoing trend to outsourcing in these sectors will provide the opportunity to add a number of new mining and civil engineering contracts to the company's order book during the new year," the company said.

Henry Walker said the company's contracting division had work on hand at June 30 of A$1 billion, a 22 percent rise on the previous year, after achieving a 16 percent rise in profit before tax in 1996/97 to A$26 million.
The company's underground mining operations generated a profit for the first time since their acquisition, although its Indonesian operations saw earnings cut to A$900,00 from A$2.1 million, it said.

Further to its 1997/98 outlook, Henry Walker said its environmental division, which has acquired the waste water treatment assets from Tubemakers of Australia, would seek to acquire several treatment contracts with a value of around A$5 million or more in 1997/98.

The company would seek to increase earnings in its transport services, which maintained revenue in 1996/97 but dropped profit to A$2.6 million from A$3.1 million, and advance restructuring of the division, it said.
Henry Walker shares were nine cents firmer at A$2.72 at 10.50 a.m. (0050 GMT). -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
